title: add jsonschema response_format with strict validation and OpenAI-compat layer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation:
Add first-class support for structured output using JSON Schema through a new response_format parameter and a strict validation mode that mirrors common OpenAI compatibility behaviors. This PR introduces server-side schema validation, improved error messages for invalid model output, SDK updates (Python + TS) to expose the new API surface, documentation and examples, and a controlled rollout path with a backward compatible fallback.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce response_format=json_schema option (server API) with optional strict=true|false.
- Server-side JSON Schema validator integrated into the generation pipeline; validation runs on final output and (best-effort) incremental validation for streaming.
- Clear structured error semantics: validation_failure, validation_error_codes, and human-readable messages that client SDKs can surface.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: add response_format to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and map errors to OpenAI-like error structures when requested.
- SDK changes: Python and TypeScript clients accept response_format and strict flags and expose typed helpers for schema-based parsing.
- Docs and examples: new guide with examples for strict vs non-strict, streaming hints, and migration notes.

Implementation notes:
- Server: api/v1/generate.go adds response_format parsing and wires a validator before response commit. The validator is schema-aware and supports refs; it is implemented as a thin wrapper around the new runtime/schema_validator module.
- Runtime: schema_validator performs final JSON Schema validation and returns a compact error report. For streaming, we emit "validation_hint" events when partial tokens are unlikely to produce a valid final document (best-effort heuristics).
- SDKs: python client now supports response_format and strict, and includes helpers to run local validation to provide nice error messages offline. Typescript client updated to include types and error surfaces.
- Backward compatibility: default behavior is identical to today (no validation). Strict mode is opt-in; in non-strict mode we still attach validation metadata but do not fail requests.

Checklist:
- [x] API schema and parsing
- [x] Server validator integration
- [x] SDK updates (python, typescript)
- [x] Unit tests (validator, API parsing)
- [x] Integration tests (OpenAI-compat endpoint)
- [x] Docs and examples

Testing and CI:
Initial CI run surfaced a flaky e2e test for streaming hints; I fixed the race by adding a deterministic seed to the streaming simulator and retried CI. All checks green on merge. Performance: validator adds ~3-6ms on average for final validation on typical schemas (benchmarked in perf-canary); we added caching for compiled schemas to reduce overhead on repeat runs.

Migration / Rollout:
- Feature is behind a runtime flag for controlled rollout.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we surface a config toggle; documentation covers recommended rollout (start non-strict, enable strict via canary).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Consider adding server-side partial-merge repair suggestions for common schema errors (follow-up RFC).
- Add dashboard metrics for validation failure rate and error classes (follow-up alerts/observability PR).

Related Linear: ENG-1024 (schema response_format), ENG-1101 (openai compat mapping)

Maya Chen: Streaming hints are best-effort; we've added a paragraph in docs clarifying they are advisory and can be absent. The streaming events include a 'validation_hint' field with confidence and reason.
Priya Patel: Please ensure the OpenAI-compat error mapping doesn't leak internal error ids. Also add a short section on backward compatibility in the docs.
Maya Chen: Updated docs, removed internal ids from the compat mapping, and added migration notes. PTAL.
Diego Ramirez: Performance looks fine in perf-canary, but add a compiled-schema cache TTL. Also please add metrics for validation_failure.rate so SRE can alert.
Maya Chen: Added compiled-schema cache with TTL and a simple metric (schema_validation.failure.count). Will follow up with dashboards in a separate PR.
Liam O'Connor: Verified unit tests and integration tests. Approving pending CI green.
CI: integration tests failed on first run due to flaky streaming test. Rerun queued.
CI: All checks passed after fix. Approving merge.
Priya Patel: Approved. Nice work on keeping the default behavior unchanged and making strict opt-in.

release_notes: Added response_format=json_schema with optional strict validation mode. Server-side validation provides structured validation errors and SDK helpers. Default behavior unchanged (opt-in strict). See docs/openai-compat/response_format.md for migration and examples.
